scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: It's the IT department office here (our machines are
the 192.168.1.x ones). None of our computers can get to anything on the
network any more -- not the shared drives, not the other departments,
nothing, and it hit all of us at the same time. A whole room does not go
dark together on its own. Someone here said it plainly: the department
switch has died. I wouldn't know which box that is or where it lives, but it
is your box and your job to find it. Check whatever connects our room to the
rest of the campus and get us back on today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** No subsystem, daemon, interface, or policy is misconfigured or faulty in the current lab state.

**Mechanism:** The helpdesk ticket reports a complete IT-department (192.168.1.x) blackout attributed to the department switch (switch0). A full end-to-end investigation found every component in the IT LAN path to be healthy and correctly configured. All five IT hosts (it_hod, it_lab1–it_lab4) hold valid static IPs in 192.168.1.0/24, carry a correct default route pointing to 192.168.1.1, and can reach that gateway, cross-campus subnets (192.168.3.x), and the internet segment (128.168.0.x) with zero packet loss.

**Localization:** switch0's bridge (br0) correctly members both eth0 (link to router0) and eth1 (IT LAN), with both ports UP and no errors or carrier transitions in the counters beyond normal startup STP convergence. Router0's eth0 carries 192.168.1.1/24 and has the subnet in the FIB as directly connected. No ACL rules, no traffic-shaping qdiscs, no duplicate MACs, no DHCP anomalies, no flap/fault-injection processes, and no resource pressure were found anywhere in the 30-device lab.

**Root cause:** There is no active or recent network fault — the IT department's reported outage cannot be reproduced or traced to any fault mechanism in the current lab state.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required on the network. The ticket should be closed as unconfirmed; if users experienced a transient event, it predates this investigation and left no traces in counters, logs, or process tables.
